races.name: Racing TV Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Leopards Rock
runners_data.note: Ran 3rd and 2nd in two starts over 7f-8f on Standard going, showing consistent form; tracks pace naturally from a prominent position which suits this unchallenged-leader setup, and Edward Bethell's yard is active with a reasonable 3/32 14-day strike rate; 13 days since last run is a normal turnaround.

runners_data.name: Star Of The Desert
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden runner with a single placing over 8f on Standard going; the STYLE_FIT flag indicates this horse is operating outside its comfort zone positionally, which tempers its outright winning chance even as it sets the pace; David Nolan takes the ride but the trainer's 0/9 14-day record offers no support.

runners_data.name: Blairtum Night
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt runner returning after 225 days off — a major concern — and finished 8th in its only start over 7f on Standard going; a tendency to fade in the finish compounds the fitness worry, making this a very difficult winning prospect unless dramatically improved.

runners_data.name: Rake Lane
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a single run to its name (7th over 7f on Standard), leaving its true profile unknown; Jack Garritty rides for Mark Walford whose 14-day figures are moderate at 2/20; lightly raced flag means any assessment of its likely position or finishing style is largely guesswork.

runners_data.name: Bella Angelina
runners_data.note: Finished 3rd on Good going over 7f, providing the most relevant similar-going evidence in the field; Harry Charlton sends this filly north with Lewis Edmunds aboard, and the step up to a mile may suit; stylistically unknown but the going form gives a small positional edge over the other unknowns.

runners_data.name: Wid
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's hold-up performer has the strongest recent form profile — 2nd over 8f on Good, 7th over 7f on Good — and Jason Hart is a high-quality booking; structurally disadvantaged by a slow, uncontested pace but the best-credentialed closer in the race if the leader fades.

races.paceDynamic: Star Of The Desert is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no other horse likely to press for the lead, will control the pace from the outset at Carlisle over a mile on Good ground. Leopards Rock is the natural stalker from a prominent position and will likely slot in just off the pace, with Bella Angelina and Rake Lane — both stylistically unknown — needing to find their places in the early stages. The hold-up horses Blairtum Night and Wid will be rearmost, though Blairtum Night carries a significant fitness concern after 225 days off and a tendency to fade in the finish. With a single, uncontested pace-setter dictating a sustainable tempo, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and strike in the straight, giving horses like Leopards Rock a structural advantage over the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of The Desert sets a steady, uncontested tempo and the race develops into a home-straight sprint.
scenarios.body: Star Of The Desert controls affairs throughout at a fair pace, and the horse tracking closest — Leopards Rock — has first run at the top of the straight, making the most of the minimal ground loss throughout; a sustained gallop over a flat mile on Good ground suits a prominent, economical traveller perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected and the leader ties up inside the final two furlongs, allowing the hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: Wid has placed twice over this sort of trip and going combination and is the most credible late challenger based on recent form and similar-going record; however, true hold-up horses are structurally disadvantaged by a lone, steady pace-setter and this scenario requires an unlikely collapse from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced, stylistically unknown runners — Bella Angelina or Rake Lane — finds a prominent position early and outstays the field.
scenarios.body: Bella Angelina has the most encouraging similar-going evidence (3rd on Good) and could benefit if she settles mid-division and improves past the leaders late; Rake Lane is 4yo and lightly raced, representing an unknown quantity, though the absence of any clear positional data makes this scenario speculative.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Star Of The Desert is allowed an even softer lead than expected and the field fails to close, letting it score from the front.
scenarios.body: This requires the pace to be genuinely slow and the field to not organise a challenge until too late — possible but unlikely given the moderate class and the fact that Leopards Rock will be tracking throughout; the STYLE_FIT flag on Star Of The Desert also tempers confidence in it winning from the front.

watchPoints.text: Watch Star Of The Desert's early fractions — if it dawdles in front unchallenged, the pace could be so slow that hold-up horses like Wid never get a meaningful opportunity to close.
Blairtum Night has been off 225 days and fades in finishes; watch for any early signs of a sloppy preparation in the paddock or sluggish early pace work that confirms it is not ready to compete.

Bella Angelina and Rake Lane are both stylistically unverified — watch how quickly they settle and where they position in the first two furlongs, as their early placement will dictate which scenario becomes live.

Leopards Rock's jockey Oisin Orr should be watched for how close he sits to Star Of The Desert — if he tracks within a length from the front, the race shape strongly aligns with Scenario A before a ball has been bowled.

Wid's trainer Ralph Beckett has a strong 14-day record (7/52) and Jason Hart's booking carries weight — watch whether Beckett has targeted this novice for improvement, which would elevate the closer scenario despite the structural disadvantage.

races.name: Molson Coors EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Muckle Handicap

runners_data.name: Wolf Of Badenoch
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with similar-going record of just one placed run from five on Good/Soft, though the 4yo's recent form shows some consistency; Stevie Donohoe rides and will likely settle wide, but winning off OR 60 requires a big step up on recent efforts.

runners_data.name: Fleur De Mer
runners_data.note: Placed twice in 15 outings on similar ground and handles 12-15f distances well; the 6yo mare has blinkers noted and Paul Mulrennan gives connections an experienced pilot, though her sim-going record (2/15, 0 wins) is a quiet concern over Good turf specifically.

runners_data.name: Is She Now
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner with a clear tactical advantage in this shape; trainer Daragh Bourke sends her out just 3 days after her last run (T14: 1/2) suggesting confidence, and two recent wins over 12-13f on Good/Soft ground underpin her as the horse to beat here — the STYLE_FIT flag reflects she is racing in role, not out of it, and should not be discounted.

runners_data.name: Ottoman
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by nature, placed out to midfield on the map because true closers overflow this field; his best recent efforts have come over 12f on Good ground (2nd and 3rd), and OR 53 looks workable if Thomas Greatrex can engineer a prominent position, though that is against his natural grain.

runners_data.name: Hijo De La Luna
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up performer whose natural style has been squeezed towards midfield by the density of closers in this field; the 6yo has visor headgear on and consistent form over 10-14f on Good, but his sim-going record (6/15, 0 wins, 1 placed) from the back is modest and Andrew Elliott will face a tactical puzzle.

runners_data.name: Broadstone
runners_data.note: Four consecutive poor finishes (9-5-4-0) with all recent runs on Tapeta make this 4yo a significant unknown on turf; John Norton's yard has one runner in the past 14 days and the horse carries the lowest OR (45) in the race — blinkers noted, but form on Good turf is simply absent. True hold-up type squeezed into the midfield map position given the field composition.

runners_data.name: Due To Shine
runners_data.note: The youngest runner at 3yo and lightest weight (118lbs), placed 3rd and 2nd earlier in his career over 8-10f on Good/Soft but has disappointed since (11th, 7th most recently); 54 days off the track is notable and Cam Hardie inherits a hold-up type whose natural rear-tracking style places him poorly in a shape dominated by a lone leader — Due To Shine is one of those mapped forward of his true preference.

races.paceDynamic: Is She Now is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just a field of seven over 1m3f at Carlisle, she is virtually guaranteed to lead from the outset at a pace she can control — no rival has the natural inclination or ability to press her. The rest of the field — Ottoman, Hijo De La Luna, Broadstone, Due To Shine, Wolf Of Badenoch, and Fleur De Mer — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning Is She Now faces zero pressure and can dictate every fraction. Several of those hold-up horses have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the field cannot accommodate that many true closers at the rear; Ottoman, Hijo De La Luna, Broadstone, and Due To Shine are the principal redistributed types, and Is She Now along with Wolf Of Badenoch are most likely to actually secure their natural positions. This race shape — a single uncontested leader carving out a controlled, sustainable gallop — strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles over true hold-up horses, whose redistributed map positions overstate how cleanly they will be able to execute their preferred late-run tactics.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Is She Now Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Is She Now leads unchallenged and dictates a measured, sustainable pace over the 1m3f trip.
scenarios.body: Is She Now has recent course-distance form (won over 13f on Good, won over 12f on Good) and sits on a workable mark of OR 52 after a 3-day turnaround suggesting trainer confidence; with no natural presser in the field, David Nolan can set every fraction and kick clear entering the straight. Prominent types who can track closely will be best placed, but the leader's rhythm is the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Is She Now sets a stronger-than-expected pace that softens the field and allows a late finisher to swoop.
scenarios.body: A genuinely fast early clip — perhaps forced by early positional jockeying from redistributed midfielders — could string the field out and leave Is She Now vulnerable inside the final furlong. Fleur De Mer and Wolf Of Badenoch, both holding OK going flags and proven at staying distances, have the profiles to pick up the pieces if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed hold-up type successfully tracks closer than expected and outstays the leader in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Ottoman has the best recent form of the bunch (2nd and 3rd over 12f on Good) and, though mapped to midfield out of role, could benefit if Nolan's lead is slightly too aggressive over this longer 1m3f; Greatrex is capable of placing a horse tactically and an early cover position could prove decisive. The scenario requires Ottoman to race genuinely out of character, which tempers its likelihood significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches — Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistributed horses push forward early, creating an unexpectedly competitive pace and a chaotic closing straight.
scenarios.body: With several horses uncomfortable settling deep, there is a small chance of a compressed, scrappy race where positional battles mid-race blunt every runner's finishing effort. In that outcome, the horse with the clearest run and most straightforward trip — likely Wolf Of Badenoch staying wide — could profit from the resulting gaps.

watchPoints.text: Is She Now's 3-day turnaround and trainer's recent 1/2 strike rate suggest live confidence — watch if she jumps cleanly and immediately dictates, as any stumble or sluggish break transforms the entire pace picture.

Ottoman, Hijo De La Luna, Broadstone, and Due To Shine are all genuine hold-up types redistributed to midfield — watch for early positional jockeying as riders attempt to secure ground they are not naturally suited to, which could create scrimmaging in the first quarter-mile.

Fleur De Mer's blinkers and Broadstone's blinkers flag possible early exuberance from each; if either breaks sharply and tracks Is She Now closer than expected, the theoretical solo lead scenario weakens materially.

Wolf Of Badenoch and Fleur De Mer both have the widest experience at staying distances in this field — watch their positioning at the half-mile marker as an indicator of whether the pace has been genuinely slow enough to set up a late run.

races.name: Rachael Bell Wealth Management Handicap

runners_data.name: Catalyse
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer trained by Jim Goldie with a modest recent string including two zeros; similar-going form is sparse (1W from 10 comparable runs) and the 7lb claimer reduces weight burden slightly, but a pattern of finishing mid-to-rear makes this shape tough for the horse.

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: The one confirmed front-runner here, last seen 14 days ago and trained by Iain Jardine who is in decent form (7/31 in 14 days); the STYLE_FIT flag notes it operates just outside its most natural role, yet as the sole pace-setter on good ground it owns the race tactically — only five comparable-going runs to draw on.

runners_data.name: Mr Cool
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners this 4yo for Charlie Johnston's well-resourced stable (9/60 T14); consistent recent form figures (2-5-6-7-5) on good ground at 6-7f suggest a genuine hold-up horse that fires regularly without always winning — suits a scenario where pace is honest enough for a late rattle.

runners_data.name: Bay Breeze
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 7yo has placed on good ground at 6f before and wears a hood; its natural style is rear-of-field, but with five other hold-up horses compressed into the same space, getting a clear run and a true pace to aim at is the central concern for Duran Fentiman.

runners_data.name: Great
runners_data.note: Sam England's 4yo has visited the frame at 6f on good ground (3rd last time out, a rare form highlight in an otherwise mid-pack recent profile); a genuine closer who needs the race to be run at a proper tempo, and the modest pace of this field is the primary headwind.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good ground just 13 days ago and has strong similar-going credentials (3W/7P from 9 runs); the tongue-tie is in place and Barry McHugh takes over — the prominent style suits this shape ideally as she can track the leader and use her finishing kick from a race-friendly position.

runners_data.name: Instant Bond
runners_data.note: Two wins from three good-ground 6f starts in recent form (1-1-3) make the going and trip combination compelling; Paul Mulrennan rides and the tongue-tie stays on — a prominent racer who can sit just off the pace and is strongly placed to feature if Mount Ruapehu's lead is catchable.

runners_data.name: Orbital Chime
runners_data.note: Helen Cuthbert's 6yo has only two comparable-going runs to draw on and wears a visor; its true running style is hold-up, and with the field stacked with rearward runners, Lewis Edmunds will need to find gaps late in a race where the pace may simply not be strong enough to bring closers into play.

runners_data.name: Henriette Ronner
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's 3yo is yet to win and has shown only one place finish from 11 recent runs, all on varying surfaces; the visor is retained, and while Tom Eaves is a capable handler of these sprint types, the lack of good-ground form (0W/0P from 2 runs) and the crowded hold-up group make this a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Kyber Crystal
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' 7yo has placed three times from 11 good-ground runs but never won on the surface; wears a tongue-tie and hood combination and is stepping up from 5f, which is a slight concern — the extra furlong may help or hinder, but the compressed closer group and OR of 51 make winning difficult.

runners_data.name: Soda
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's 3yo has only four career runs, three of which placed, including a 3rd at 6f on good ground; stepping back from further trips is a positive angle and William Pyle takes over, but this is a hold-up type whose inexperience and low OR of 53 leave it vulnerable in an 11-runner field with a congested rear group.

races.paceDynamic: Mount Ruapehu is the one confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f handicap and, with no confirmed rival willing to press from the outside, is likely to enjoy a genuinely uncontested lead through the early stages on good ground at Carlisle. Miss Rainbow and Instant Bond are the next most forward-going types and will look to sit just off the pace in the prominent positions, creating a moderate but not pressurised tempo that will likely be steady enough to suit those racing close to the speed. The race shape strongly favours prominent and close-up runners who can track the leader without burning energy — a true late-closer's finish is unlikely given the lack of genuine pace injection from behind. Bay Breeze, Henriette Ronner, Orbital Chime, Kyber Crystal and Soda are all natural hold-up horses whose true rearward positions have been displaced onto the map by sheer volume of similar types — of these, Miss Rainbow and Instant Bond are most likely to actually secure the forward berths they need, while the genuine closers will face a stiffer challenge than usual to reel in a relaxed leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Ruapehu bowls along unchallenged and sets an honest but controlled gallop, allowing it to conserve energy through the turn.
scenarios.body: Mount Ruapehu controls the tempo throughout, and with no rival willing to commit to a sustained challenge early, the prominent pair tracking it are best placed to capitalise; horses who travel smoothly close to the pace without over-racing on the good surface are the beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Ruapehu's early lead draws Miss Rainbow and Instant Bond into a tracking position that allows them to quicken past the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace proves sustainable enough that Miss Rainbow and Instant Bond, sitting a length or two off the leader, have a clear sightline and finish past a tiring front-runner; both have form at this trip on good ground and their prominent profiles are perfectly suited.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Ruapehu goes just fast enough to string the field out early and the hold-up horses find more room than expected on the wide Carlisle straight.
scenarios.body: Mr Cool and Great, genuine hold-up types with course-and-distance form on good ground, would be the main beneficiaries if a slightly stronger pace opens a late gap; however, the redistribution of multiple closers means competition for running room is fierce and the probability of this shape fully unfolding is tempered.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that Mount Ruapehu simply lopes clear in the final two furlongs and none of the closers can close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: A crawl in the early stages leaves every hold-up horse with too much ground to make up in just six furlongs; Mount Ruapehu, already relaxed on a clean lead, simply extends and the field cannot produce a late burst on a flat, sound surface.

watchPoints.text: Mount Ruapehu goes to post as the sole front-runner — watch whether Andrew Mullen elects to bowl along at a true pace or allows the gallop to drift very slow, as the tempo he sets will define every other runner's race.

Miss Rainbow and Instant Bond will both try to secure prominent positions behind the leader — watch the first two furlongs for any scrimmaging between them, as the loser of that early position battle faces a significantly harder task from further back.

Bay Breeze, Orbital Chime, Henriette Ronner, Kyber Crystal and Soda are all natural hold-up horses competing for the same late-closing ground — watch for traffic and interference in the final two furlongs as five horses converge on limited space.

Instant Bond's two recent wins at this exact trip and going combination on a flat track make him the standout form angle — watch whether Mulrennan is able to slot in just off Miss Rainbow in the early stages rather than being forced wider or further back.

Great and Mr Cool both have recent placed form at 6f on good ground and are trained by handlers in decent recent strike rates — watch both for sustained late momentum if the pace quickens entering the final two furlongs.

races.name: British EBF Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Mae Amor
runners_data.note: Won over 6f good at Carlisle recently which is directly relevant form, though her hold-up style is the tactical concern in a race where the gallop may not be strong enough to set her alight from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Ormolulu
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with solid placed form at 6f on good going, but her natural inclination to race from behind is harder to execute here — the mapped midfield slot overstates where she will likely travel, and the slow pace shape does her no favours.|

runners_data.name: Cotai Belle
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter whose recent 2nd-2nd placed form over this exact course-trip-going combination shows she handles these conditions; Richard & Fahey in good form (T14: 5/52) and the 3yo filly racing against older rivals.|

runners_data.name: D Flawless
runners_data.note: Won at 6f on good going last time out and carries useful form, but her true preference is to race from the rear — placed at midfield by the tool because too many hold-up types compete for those slots, meaning she will likely race in a position that doesn't fully suit.|

runners_data.name: Rogue Attraction
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell filly whose win at 6f on good ground and placed 2nd at 6f good earlier in the year gives her strong pace-fit credentials; the patient hood (hg:p) and a sharp jockey booking in Oisin Orr suggest she is primed for a bold show from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Bleep Test
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is in prolific form (T14: 15/104) and this prominent racer suits the race shape well, sitting close to Cotai Belle throughout and getting the benefit of first run inside the final two furlongs; the 0 last time was a blot but she placed four times previously.|

runners_data.name: Dandy Magic
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago which is a notable freshness concern, and her good-going form at this trip is limited — she is a natural hold-up filly competing in a race where that style is crowded out, and the very recent run adds extra doubt about peak readiness.|

runners_data.name: Creative Queen
runners_data.note: William Haggas, who is in strong form (T14: 10/56), runs this 3yo filly who placed twice at 6f and won at 6f on soft, giving her course-trip experience; the blinkers (hg:b) suggest she needs a switch and the prominent-leaning style could mean she travels sweetly in the slipstream of Cotai Belle.|

races.paceDynamic: Cotai Belle is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in this 8-runner 6f handicap on good ground, she should control tempo at a measured, sustainable gallop from the outset. Bleep Test is the only other horse likely to race prominently, providing a secondary presence without threatening to disrupt Cotai Belle's rhythm. This is a single-pace scenario where the leader dictates throughout — that setup classically rewards prominent racers who can track the gallop and pounce inside the final furlong, rather than hold-up horses who need a truly strong pace to generate the late gap. Several hold-up types — Ormolulu, D Flawless, and Dandy Magic — are genuine come-from-behind runners who cannot realistically secure their preferred rear position in this field and have been mapped to midfield accordingly; of those three, D Flawless (shortest recent trip, best recent form) and Ormolulu (class and experience at 6f good) are most likely to carve out a realistic midfield spot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cotai Belle Controls, Closest Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Belle sets a comfortable lead and the race is run at an honest but uncontested tempo, horses tracking her closely through the race have first run.
scenarios.body: Cotai Belle's lone front-running role at a sustainable clip means the race is set up for those who sit second or third and have the speed to overhaul her in the closing stages; Bleep Test, pressing her throughout, and Creative Queen, likely to travel prominently on debut for Haggas over this course-and-distance combination, are ideally positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Cotai Belle is allowed to bowl along at a generous gallop that nobody accelerates past, she simply conserves enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: Uncontested leaders on good ground over 6f at Carlisle can be remarkably hard to peg back, and Cotai Belle's recent placed form over exactly this course and distance suggests she handles these conditions well; with no horse willing or able to pressurise her, she runs the others ragged by doing nothing wrong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Emerge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns out sharper than expected and the front horses burn out, horses settled in midfield with a late turn of foot grab the advantage.
scenarios.body: Mae Amor won over this course and distance in recent form and has the profile to come from off the pace if the gallop stretches things out; Rogue Attraction won over 6f on good going and is capable of finishing powerfully if a gap appears in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Hold-Up Types Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the true hold-up horses — Ormolulu, D Flawless, Dandy Magic — secure their natural rear position and the pace collapses through the field.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially discounted because all three are tagged as redistributed — they are unlikely to get a genuine held-up berth against this pace shape, and their style-fit scores signal they will be racing out of their comfort zone; even if one does slot in late, the uncontested tempo makes a fast-finishing surge unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Cotai Belle — watch whether she is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead from the gates; if nothing challenges her in the first two furlongs, her chance of staying on to at least place increases markedly and changes the complexion of every other scenario.

Dandy Magic — ran just three days ago and is the most obviously time-short runner in the field; if she weakens before the final furlong she may cause interference for any midfield horse attempting a late run down the inner rail.

D Flawless, Ormolulu, and Dandy Magic — all three are natural hold-up types competing for rear positions that the race shape cannot accommodate; watch whether any of them over-race or fail to settle when pushed wider into midfield earlier than they prefer.

Creative Queen — the fitting of blinkers for William Haggas is worth tracking from the stalls; if she jumps sharply and slots into second or third behind Cotai Belle, she moves immediately into the most dangerous prominent tracking position in the race.

Rogue Attraction — Oisin Orr's positioning from the gate is worth watching; if he gets a clean break and sits fourth or fifth with cover, she has the good-going 6f form to mount a serious challenge in the closing stages and becomes the most interesting closer in the field.

races.name: Dalston 'Confined' Handicap

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up specialist with very limited recent form (three 9ths in last five), whose true style means this slow-pace scenario may never allow him to land a meaningful blow from deep — sim-going record of just one place from 15 runs on comparable ground is damning.

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who steps back up to 7f after a string of 6f runs, and the addition of headgear-like hold-up tactics on Good ground at Carlisle give faint hope if the race opens late; one place in ten similar-going runs suggests improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Record Day
runners_data.note: Holds a course-relevant profile having placed at 6f and 7f on Good ground before, and the 5lb claimer Conor Whiteley gives a small weight relief; his true racing style is to hold up, meaning this compressed-pace scenario asks him to work harder than he might prefer.

runners_data.name: Fan Mail
runners_data.note: Arrives fresh on just 5 days' rest for Tim Easterby, a yard with a solid strike rate, and while Fan Mail's hold-up instincts are genuine, the crowded rear of the field in this pace shape means he is more likely to race mid-division than secure his natural position — best watched for a strong late run in a scenario that never quite arrives.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: Veteran handler Katie Scott sends this five-year-old who holds four places in seven 7f runs on comparable ground, and crucially he has the tactical versatility to race prominently enough behind Homestrait to make his mark — his hold-up tag is slightly flattering; he often races closer than pure closers and that suits this shape.

runners_data.name: Judicature
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse whose best effort recently was a second at 7f on Soft — the trip and conditions are fine, but being squeezed into midfield by the redistribution effect means Tom Eaves will need to find an opening that may never materialise in a compressed-pace event; limited sim-going returns (no wins in ten) reinforce caution.

runners_data.name: Albeseeingyer
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr takes the ride for Steph Hollinshead on a horse with an excellent similar-going profile (1 win, 4 places from 15 runs), and despite being a genuine hold-up type by nature, 24 days off and a strong form line at this trip on Good give him claims if he can get a prominent-enough berth by default in this redistributed field.

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: The race-shaping horse — Brian Ellison's three-year-old has placed in four of his last five at this trip on Good ground and goes on this surface well, and Cam Hardie should be able to dictate terms completely; the STYLE_FIT note tempers the very highest expectations but the tactical advantage of setting an uncontested pace is clear.

runners_data.name: Dakota Breeze
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's three-year-old arrives on a career-best ground profile (only one similar-going run on record) and has shown speed enough to place at 7f before, but zero wins and a field full of horses competing for what little early position exists make this a tough ask from a redistributed midfield berth.

runners_data.name: Sailor's Return
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner returns quickly (6 days) after a 6th at 7f on Good, and while the trainer's 14-day strike rate is reasonable, consecutive moderate efforts (two 6ths, a 4th) on this trip suggest he is finding his level; a natural hold-up style in a falsely-run race is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Supreme Clarets
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's three-year-old was a runner-up at 7f on Good as recently as this season, which is the most encouraging form line in the field for a closer — however, he is pushed into midfield by the redistribution effect and Warren Fentiman takes over on the 3lb claimer, adding a small positional uncertainty to what is otherwise a live place contender in an open scenario.

runners_data.name: Top Lad
runners_data.note: An 85-day absence is the headline concern here, and while Michael and David Easterby occasionally produce first-run winners, only one placing in six runs on comparable going and an inexperienced 7lb claimer in Lewis Chalkley makes this look an unlikely winning vehicle in a competitive 12-runner handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Homestrait is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 7f handicap on Good ground at Carlisle, and with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, Cam Hardie can dictate terms at a comfortable, controlled tempo without being pressured into burning early energy. The absence of a pace duel means the race is likely to be run at a measured, sustainable gallop, compressing the field and making the race more of a test of cruising speed and a late change of gear than raw stamina. This shape strongly favours runners who can travel prominently in behind the leader or just off the pace, ready to pounce entering the final two furlongs — hold-up horses coming from deep will face a wall of horses in a falsely-run race and are unlikely to generate the momentum they need. This field carries significantly more genuine hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Dakota Breeze, Judicature, Albeseeingyer, Supreme Clarets, Fan Mail and others are natural closers who will be forced to race closer to the pace than ideal, meaning Homestrait's primary pursuers in reality will be horses that can sit a length or two off the leader and time a run, rather than true hold-up operators.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Homestrait Controls, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Homestrait is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a fair-to-moderate pace that suits the leader throughout.
scenarios.body: Cam Hardie dictates every yard from the front on Good ground where Homestrait's solid recent form (three placings in last four) counts for plenty, and a compressed field unable to quicken from deep means the leader simply kicks again in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Stalker Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or mid-division runner travels smoothly just off Homestrait's pace and produces a decisive late burst in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With the tempo controlled and gaps opening on the wide Carlisle straight, a horse sitting two or three lengths off the pace has the ideal platform to pick up off a true gallop and collar the front-runner near the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise on Fade
scenarios.trigger: If Homestrait sets a faster-than-expected pace and ties up inside the final furlong, opening the door for closers.
scenarios.body: In this less likely shape, the modest pace suddenly accelerates mid-race as horses push forward, stretching the field and allowing genuine hold-up horses to find daylight late — but this requires a collapse at the front that the current evidence does not strongly support.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rough Race, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches tightly mid-race due to the slow pace and positional jostling causes interference, producing a messy sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With so many horses forced out of their natural positions — true hold-up types racing in mid-division, jostling for room — a chaotic straight scramble becomes possible, favouring any horse that finds a clear run and has the raw ability to finish best.

watchPoints.text: Homestrait (Cam Hardie) must be monitored in the stalls and at the break — if anything rushes him into a faster-than-intended pace in the opening furlong, the entire race shape flips and hold-up horses gain relevance immediately.

Albeseeingyer and Judicature are both genuine hold-up horses competing for similar late-race real estate — if they are both squeezed wide or blocked in mid-division, the closers' scenario collapses entirely and the front of the race becomes even more dominant.

Supreme Clarets has the standout form line for a hold-up horse (second at 7f on Good this season) and should not be dismissed lightly despite being mapped mid-division — watch for Warren Fentiman to angle wide early to secure racing room.
Black Storm's weight of 141lbs is the highest in the field — if this becomes a test of stamina late in the 7f, the extra burden could blunt his finish even if he travels well through the race.

Fan Mail's quick reappearance (5 days) for Tim Easterby is worth monitoring at the start — horses returning quickly for this yard sometimes show above-expected freshness, and if Fan Mail breaks sharply he could secure a better position than his redistribution tag suggests.
